summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloblastic leukemia in remission, chronic graft-versus-host disease, cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation. He presented with worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, and lightheadedness. Evaluation revealed volume overload without active infection, as blood and urine cultures were negative. A heart catheterization showed no significant coronary artery disease but confirmed elevated cardiac pressures. He was treated with intravenous diuresis, optimized heart failure medications, and close monitoring of renal function. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged home on oral diuretics, beta-blockers, and ACE inhibitors with plans for close outpatient follow-up and home health monitoring.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure
